### Round 2

The hard part is probably working out each brick's landing layer: the highest filled cell under its footprint. The task also needs a check that every cell the brick fills is still missing and that the brick seals no missing cells beneath it. So the nets so far need a strong per-layer bias. This round tests: (a) a 1-epoch recipe on the round-1 residual CNN, giving about 3.3× the starting sample count; (b) a net that reads each height layer as a token, run with the 2-epoch recipe; and (c) the same layer-token net with the 1-epoch recipe.

### Round 3
All six trials score 0 on dev and 0 on training success. The failures are no-learning, not timeouts or check failures, so the problem is learning itself. Every head so far assumes the described action layout, with per-cell, translation-equivariant logits that are aligned to spec.footprints. The task warns the world may differ. If the action indexing differs (for example transposed axes, a different anchor, or swapped types), every conv head would map features to the wrong cells and learning would stall, which matches what we see. ### Round 4
Nine trials, two seeds each, all scored 0 on both dev success and training success. None failed a check or timed out, and all ran in 38–260 s. So the bottleneck is learning itself, not generalisation. The flat-head diagnostic also stayed at 0. That makes a mismatched action layout an unlikely sole cause, but it does not rule one out. With no positive signal there is nothing to refine, and the starting architecture stays selected unless a candidate scores above 0.
